Atlas Copco.why: its Vacuum Technique business area supplies vacuum pumps and abatement systems installed with semiconductor process tools; semi orders drove record group order intake
Atlas Copco.evidence: Atlas Copco Q2 FY2026 call (07-16-2026): CEO - Vacuum Technique orders +59% organic, semi orders from advanced and mature nodes; new abatement system for the semiconductor market; some factories must more than double output

players.product: vacuum pumps and exhaust abatement systems for semiconductor fabs (Vacuum Technique business area)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026: record order intake, organic orders +26%; revenue +8% organic; adjusted profit +12% with a margin of 21%; operating margin 20.6%; return on capital employed 24%; more than SEK 10 billion added to the order book; profit before tax SEK 9.1 billion (SEK 8.4 billion); cash flow SEK 6.8 billion. Year-to-date orders received SEK 96 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: orders organic +26%; revenue organic +8%; operating margin 20.6%

quarterly_data.signal: Vacuum Technique: orders +59% organic, now 25% of group orders over the last 12 months. CEO: semiconductor orders came from all the major markets, from advanced nodes and mature nodes, with China very strong; growth is broad-based across all players and regions including the U.S.; industrial and scientific vacuum also grew (batteries, metallurgy, research). Most orders have firm delivery dates; some pre-ordering, but not huge.

Vacuum Technique ramp-up: CFO - semi demands are 'very extraordinary' and in certain factories output must more than double to meet customer demand, which requires investment in direct labor and costs that dilute drop-through; CEO - 'all hands on deck to increase the output of our factories', the ramp-up is going to plan, the priority is to keep competitive lead times in semi. The Genesee factory in the Buffalo area is coming online gradually and will be ramped step by step in coming quarters.

Near-term outlook (sequential, next quarter): customer activity increased from Q1 to Q2 and is expected to remain at that elevated level, supported by continued strong semi and a strong general industrial market. CFO: Vacuum Technique margin is expected to improve in the coming quarter and continue improving gradually with volume.

Pricing is positive in all business areas including semi, a market where like-for-like prices used to fall year over year (CFO); faster output and competitive lead times are meant to support pricing. Vacuum Technique launched a new abatement system for semiconductor customers with better efficiency and extended mean time between services.

CEO on WFE: advanced packaging is now a significant component of WFE and Atlas Copco is well positioned, not losing competitive position; vacuum systems are installed after the process tools arrive at a fab and have shorter lead times than the tools, so timing differs from WFE spending.

Other business areas, Q2 2026: Compressor Technique orders +19% organic, revenue +3% organic, margin 24.1%, Gas and Process orders above 15% of CT orders (LNG vessels, on-site LNG, industrial gases); Industrial Technique +11% organic, margin 17.1%, including assembly tools for data-center racks; Power Technique +14% organic. Five acquisitions were completed in the quarter (including LACO Technologies, leak detection) and AeroClimate was announced.
